title: Grateful Dead Live at Starlight Theater on 1982-08-03
source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> PCM -> Dat -> CD

ai_review.summary: Crisp Miller soundboard captures a high‑energy 8/3/82 show with smoking Half‑Step Mississippi → Franklin’s, stellar To Lay Me Down and a powerhouse Big Railroad Blues.
ai_review.review: The recording is a Miller SBD that sounds clear and balanced overall, though listeners note a need for a little extra bass, occasional pitch quirks and a brief loss of level in Stella Blue. Musically the concert is a “barn‑burner” – Jerry’s solos are on fire, Brent’s keys shine through Shakedown Street and The Other One, and the band delivers tight, high‑octane versions of Mississippi Half‑Step, Franklin’s Tower, To Lay Me Down, Althea, Peggy‑O, Cumberland Blues, Big Railroad Blues, He’s Gone and Stella Blue.

ai_rating.rationale: 20 reviews with an average of 3.9 stars; the majority are 4‑5 ★ praising both performance and sound, only a few note technical flaws or mixed feelings.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear Miller SBD; some reviewers mention needing more bass, pitch‑correction (-1.5 % to -2 %) on early songs, occasional level drop in Stella Blue and a brief cut, but overall the mix is balanced with good separation.

poor_songs: Althea (noted as sluggish by one reviewer)
Cassidy (mentioned with a couple of bum notes)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong opening half‑step into Franklin’s, solid first set with classic mid‑tempo numbers; second set builds momentum with Shakedown Street jam, Samson & Delilah, Let It Grow and a soaring The Other One before closing on a high note.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for scorching solos, perfect tone, ripping Big Railroad Blues and “ripping” throughout; noted as the night’s focal point.
band_member_comments.Phil: Commended for dropping bombs on He's Gone and staying in sync with Jerry; a single comment calls his playing lackluster on Cumberland but overall solid.
band_member_comments.Bob: Acknowledged for a fiery slide break in Minglewood Blues and steady rhythm work throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent’s (or Keith’s) contributions highlighted on Shakedown Street, Samson & Delilah, The Other One and overall keyboard textures; praised as “great sound of his own”.
band_member_comments.Drums: The four‑song pre‑drums sequence in the second set is called “money”; drums described as tight and driving.
